title: Prime-avoiding positive annihilators force an additive group to vanish
statement: Let V be an additive abelian group. Suppose that for every prime natural number p there exists a natural number m such that m > 0, p does not divide m, and m • v = 0 for every v in V. Then every element of V equals zero. No finiteness assumption on V is required.
lean_statement: ∀ {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V], (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ ¬ p ∣ m ∧ ∀ v : V, m • v = 0) → ∀ v : V, v = 0
